$comment: Single source of truth for every analytics event name shipped anywhere in the platform (backend track()/ingest() calls, both Flutter apps' AnalyticsEvents constants, website). Checked by scripts/check-analytics-events.cjs, which fails a deploy if code uses an event string not listed here (docs/analytics-events.json) — this is what would have caught the 2026-07-22 silent subscription-funnel rename before it shipped. 'source' is 'server' (emitted in-process via track(), never touches the gateway's /api/events route) or 'client' (sent by an app/website via ingest(), and therefore the set the gateway's /api/events allowlist is built from). Retired events are kept here, flagged retired, so historical rows remain queryable and the checker doesn't complain about old code that no longer exists.

attendance_saas_reengagement_sent.notes: attendance-SaaS wedge — nudge sent to a gym-linked signup with no booking/subscription activity

attendance_saas_bill_charged.notes: admin applied a gym's monthly attendance-SaaS bill — users joined that month x flat per-user fee debited from the partner wallet (negative balance allowed)

partner_bank_settlement_recorded.notes: admin marked a partner's pending attendance-SaaS bank settlement as paid (manual bank transfer, outside the app)

trainer_account_created.notes: partner created a gym-employed trainer account

training_session_logged.notes: trainer self-logged which attended customer booking they trained

food_photo_on_device.notes: the on-device matcher was engaged for a photo (customer app). props matched (bool), score, runner_up, catalogue_size, model — NEVER the matched food's name, because a plate is a description of somebody's diet and the no-PII rule on health_food_photo_recognized applies to this event for the same reason. This is the calibration signal for the mobileclip drop-in: matched=false with a high score means the short-circuit bar is tuned too low (near-misses are topping the index with wrong rows), matched=true with a low runner_up means the win is decisive, and a rising catalogue_size should flatten the correlation between scores and ground truth. Server-side recognizes still fire health_food_photo_recognized; this event exists so an on-device short-circuit is visible in the same funnel without faking a model recognition

referral_credited.notes: fires when a referred customer's first completed booking triggers the ₹50/₹50 wallet credit

attendance_slot_mismatch_confirmed.notes: fires instead of attendance_verified when a partner scans a booking's QR before its session window opens and confirms shifting the slot time

badge_earned.notes: gamification wave 1 — fires on selfCheckIn when this is the customer's first-ever attended booking at gymId

wallet_topup_config_updated.notes: admin edits WalletTopupConfig (presets/allowCustomAmount/min/max) via phool-gobhi-admin's Settings page

subscription_purchased_wallet.notes: replaces the retired two-step subscription_order_created/subscription_purchased flow as of commit b8c7251

subscription_order_created.notes: superseded by subscription_purchased_wallet; historical rows only

subscription_purchased.notes: superseded by subscription_purchased_wallet; historical rows only

referral_shared.notes: Share your code tapped on the Refer & Earn screen

map_explored_opened.notes: gamification wave 1 — fog-of-war explore map opened

session_started.notes: as of 2026-08-15, the website's copy also carries properties.channel ('direct'|'organic_search'|'social'|'referral'|'campaign:<utm_source>'), referrer_host, utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content, and landing_path — captured once at the very first paint of the session, before any client-side navigation — backing the admin's traffic-source breakdown

update_required_shown.notes: force-update splash screen shown (min version gate)

onboarding_step_completed.notes: partner app: wizard page done. Customer app (since 2026-10-01): step done — props step (details|training|health_basics|why_here|medical_docs|permissions), surface (signup|resume|profile_edit), plus the step's enum answers only (currently_works_out, training_location, weekly_frequency, free_time_window); never DOB, gender or free text; the health-profile steps (since 2026-10-01) carry only step, surface and skipped (bool), never any health answer

onboarding_step_viewed.notes: customer onboarding step shown — props step, surface. Viewed minus completed per step is the drop-off

onboarding_permission_result.notes: customer onboarding permission step resolved — props permission (location|notifications), granted (bool)

onboarding_completed.notes: customer onboarding finished (signup wizard done, or the training branch saved from the resume prompt / Profile) — props surface, currently_works_out, training_location

gym_image_uploaded.notes: wired to GymScreenCubit.addImage on 2026-08-17 — previously reserved but unwired since 2026-07-23

gym_doc_uploaded.notes: wired to GymScreenCubit.addDoc on 2026-08-17 — previously reserved but unwired since 2026-07-23

gym_profile_updated.notes: wired to GymScreenCubit.updateGym on 2026-08-17 — previously reserved but unwired since 2026-07-23

dashboard_viewed.notes: wired to HomeScreenTwo.initState on 2026-08-17 — previously reserved but unwired since 2026-07-23

booking_checked_in.notes: wired to CameraCubit's QR-scan verify-attendance success on 2026-08-17 (properties.method = 'qr_scan'|'qr_scan_slot_shift') — previously reserved but unwired since 2026-07-23

gym_switched.notes: SelectedGymCubit.selectGym, only fires on an actual change of selection — backs multi-gym engagement visibility, which had zero analytics coverage before this

gym_class_created.notes: new recurring-class supply feature (ClassesCubit.addClass); properties.pending reflects whether it needs gobhi approval like other gym edits

logout_tapped.notes: fires before AuthCubit.onTapSignOut/reset() so the event still carries the outgoing user's distinct_id

cta_clicked.notes: generic CTA click event, properties.cta identifies which one (e.g. 'whatsapp', 'signup')

location_resolved.notes: fires once per session after the site's silent geolocation grab settles. properties.permission is 'granted'|'denied'|'unsupported'|'timeout'|'error'; when granted, properties.nearest_gym_distance_km is the TRUE nearest-gym distance computed server-side (no 40km discovery cutoff) — backs the admin Location Reach view

offline_shown.notes: the app-wide no-internet screen was shown (OfflineGate) — how often a transport failure interrupts someone mid-task

app_error.notes: a handled client-side error surfaced to the user

sprout_encountered.notes: map collectible came into range on the Explore map

delete_account_confirmed.notes: partner confirmed account deletion. Constant is declared but not yet wired to a call site — registered so the name is reserved and the checker stays green

run_start_viewed.notes: run tracker Start screen opened — props gps_ready, has_weight (run-tracker-spec.html §13)

run_permission_result.notes: location/notification/precise-location permission prompt resolved — props kind, result

run_started.notes: recording began — props type (run/walk/cycle), gps_ready_at_start, countdown_on

run_recovered.notes: app relaunched into the "resume your run?" sheet after an OS kill/crash — props choice (resume/finish/discard), gap_s

run_finished.notes: hold-to-finish completed — props type, distance_m, moving_s, had_gap

run_upload_failed.notes: pending-queue upload attempt failed — props attempt, http_status

health_report_uploaded.notes: a medical report was uploaded to the vault. props fileName (filename only, never contents), status=PENDING at upload time — later processing status changes are NOT re-emitted, this event marks the upload moment only

health_consent_granted.notes: base Health+ consent granted — the parent of the per-scope grants (health_medical_consent_granted, health_nutrition_consent_granted) and the legal basis for holding anything in the vault. props version = the policy version asserted, platform = ios|android. This row was written to Prisma without ever being emitted, so the funnel showed zero health opt-ins while consents existed

health_consent_revoked.notes: base Health+ consent withdrawn, which cascades to every ledger scope. The counterpart to health_consent_granted and the event to watch for churn: a revoke here means the whole health surface is off for that user

health_nutrition_consent_granted.notes: nutrition scope granted. props version = the privacy-policy version the client asserted it was showing, so a build that consents on behalf of copy it never displayed is visible here rather than in a support ticket

health_nutrition_consent_revoked.notes: nutrition scope withdrawn. props purged (true = the collected food logs were also deleted). A revoke is a churn signal; purged=true is the one to look at hardest

health_medical_consent_granted.notes: medical-records scope granted, independently of nutrition. No props: the words of the consent are not an analytics property

health_medical_consent_revoked.notes: medical-records scope withdrawn. props purged. Kept separate from the nutrition revoke because the two scopes are granted and withdrawn independently, and folding them together would make a partial withdrawal invisible

health_intake_saved.notes: target intake accepted. props skipped, hasGoal, weightWritten — shape only, never the values. A body weight is not an analytics property. Does NOT fire on a refusal; see health_targets_pace_rejected

health_targets_pace_rejected.notes: the requested loss pace was refused as unsafe, so nothing was saved. props code, limited_by ('max_weekly_loss_0.75kg'|'max_weekly_loss_pct_body_weight' — which bound actually fired), weeks_needed, max_weekly_loss_kg. The highest-signal event in this feature: it separates 'users ask for goals we decline' from 'users abandon the wizard', and limited_by shows whether our own cap is the constraint

health_target_recomputed.notes: targets recalculated from current weight. props written, skipped

health_prescription_saved.notes: the user committed the adjustable plan (calories/steps/sleep/sessions) from the app's Your plan screen. props adjusted, had_workout. Shape only and deliberately so: a calorie target and a sleep window are health data, and this dictionary is read by everyone who can query the analytics database. `adjusted` is whether the server had to move any of the four back into its legal range - a rate that climbs says our bounds and people's expectations have drifted apart, which is the one thing about this feature worth watching. Preview drags emit nothing: they are a question, not a commitment, and counting them would make a slider someone explored look like a plan someone chose.

health_food_added.notes: a gobhi reviewer added a food to the curated catalogue (the ONLY sanctioned FoodItem write in the service, by design). props source, verified, resolved_requests — source is the provenance the reviewer chose (estimate unless a real one was in hand), verified is whether they clicked the sourced-numbers box, resolved_requests is how many pending requests the add closed, which is the demand backlog turning into supply. The food's own NAME is deliberately not carried, matching health_food_requested's reasoning in reverse: a request name is what customers could not find (demand), a held catalogue row is not a data point about any one user. See foodRequestService.js's header for why this is the one sanctioned path

health_food_embeddings_refreshed.notes: a gobhi reviewer regenerated the on-device food matcher's embeddings (POST /admin/food-embeddings/refresh). props computed, model — how many curated rows were embedded and by which Gemini model, so a bad build (few rows, or the deployment accidentally keyed on a deprecated model) is visible in the admin refresh log rather than surfacing as silent customer-side match misses

health_food_logged.notes: food(s) added to a day. Three shapes on one event so foods-logged is a single funnel with an origin split, not three events that have to be summed correctly by hand. Search path: props slot, source='search' (one food). Saved-meal repeat path: props slot, source='saved_meal', logged_count, skipped_count — a repeat writes many foods in one request, so counting it as a single food would understate the feature, and skipped_count > 0 means foods left the catalogue after the meal was saved and the user was shown a partial-write warning. Photo path: props slot, source='photo_confirmed', logged_count — one photo can produce several foods, for the same reason as the repeat path

health_food_requested.notes: a user could not find a food in the picker and submitted it. props name. Fires only on CREATION, not on a repeat ask for a dish already requested — requestCount on the row is the demand signal, and counting both would make one persistent user look like growing demand. The volume and the shape of these names are the catalogue growth backlog: this is the only place that records what people actually searched for and did not find, as opposed to a guess about what they eat. Note the name IS carried — unlike a food photo's proposed names, a food name is not a description of somebody's diet, and the whole value of the event is knowing which dish

health_food_photo_recognized.notes: a food photo was recognised. props is_food, matched_count, unmatched_count — never the proposed food names, because a plate is a description of somebody's diet and this dictionary is queryable by anyone with analytics access. unmatched_count is the interesting one: a high rate means our catalogue is the bottleneck rather than the vision model, which is a different fix. Fires for a photo with no food in it too (is_food=false), so recognition attempts and recognitions are distinguishable

health_food_photo_confirmed.notes: the user confirmed foods from a photo. props slot, logged_count, corrections, rejected_count. The launch metric lives here: corrections / logged_count is the share of lines the user had to fix, and the schema comment on FoodLog.photoCorrections names half of that as the point where the feature stops earning its per-photo cost. Emitted as a funnel event rather than left to a dashboard because a cost decision needs a number that cannot quietly stop being collected

health_saved_meal_created.notes: a day's slot snapshotted as a reusable meal. props slot, line_count. A distinct decision from logging a food, and the one that predicts repeat use — a create with no later repeat is the drop-off

health_plan_regenerated.notes: suggested plan rebuilt. props created, dropped

health_day_closed.notes: a day was finalised. props frozen (false = the day was already closed, so the call was a no-op)

health_medical_doc_uploaded.notes: a medical document was stored. props kind only — never the filename, storage path, or contents; a path is a capability and the document is the user's private data

health_doctor_appointment_recorded.notes: an appointment was added to the plan. props NONE, deliberately: a doctor, a speciality, a date and a note are all health data, and the analytics util's no-PII rule applies with nothing to trade against. Fires on create only — editing an appointment is a correction, not a new booking, and re-emitting it would inflate the count of appointments a user has. Renamed from doctor_appointment_recorded at registration: this was the only health-service event without the health_ prefix, and it was renamed rather than registered as-is because it had never shipped, so no historical rows change meaning. A bare doctor_appointment prefix would also have read as the AI prescription kind of the same name, which is a different thing entirely and is explicitly rejected as a plan item kind

attendance_recorded.notes: a check-in was folded into the unified AttendanceEventLog that drives weekly streaks. props checkin_source (booking | member_checkin | self_checkin), gym_id, booking_id, member_attendance_id, already_recorded, coins_awarded. Named checkin_source rather than source because a prop called source shadows the envelope's own source field in the console sink's log line. The most important row in the gamification layer: qualifyingCheckinsPerWeek is tuned against distinct_ids per week here, and already_recorded=true rows are retries of booking-service's fire-and-forget call rather than new visits, so counting them as visits would overstate the funnel

challenge_enrolled.notes: props challenge_id, already_enrolled, target_count, reward_coins. Top of the challenge funnel. already_enrolled=true is the app re-opening a challenge the user already joined, including an abandoned one (enrollService returns any existing row as-is), so it must never be counted as a new join

challenge_left.notes: props challenge_id, prior_status, abandoned, progress_count. abandoned=false means the enrollment was already completed or left, a deliberate non-action. Abandon rate read together with progress_count is the honest signal for whether a challenge was too hard rather than boring

challenge_checkpoint_visited.notes: a checkpoint scan attempt on an outside_gym_city quest. props challenge_id, replayed, accepted, reason (enrollment_not_active | already_visited | null), progress_after, target_count, completed. Both non-accept paths are recorded on purpose: they are the anti-replay defence working, and a high already_visited share means users are re-scanning banked spots instead of finding new ones

challenge_completed.notes: props challenge_id, progress_count, target_count, reward_coins, via (checkpoint | off_peak). via separates a completion the user drove from one the off-peak rule granted on their behalf, which is a much weaker engagement signal

challenge_off_peak_advanced.notes: props challenge_count, completed_count. Emitted only when at least one off-peak challenge actually advanced, since the common case is a no-op and logging those would bury the signal. Moving visits into quiet hours is the entire point of the mechanic, so challenge_count per check-in is the number to watch

streak_viewed.notes: props current_streak, longest_streak. Streak length is an engagement metric, deliberately carrying no attendance timestamps or body measurements, consistent with the health-service entries

streak_week_resulted.notes: one row per user per closed week. props week_start, qualified, current_streak, checkin_count. This is the retention series: consecutive qualified weeks is the product's core promise, and checkin_count is what separates a user who missed the week from one who came once

streak_week_closed.notes: one anonymous row per close-week cron run (distinct_id null by design, the run is the subject and not any user). props week_start, weeks_closed, qualified, broken. A missing or short row means the cron did not fire, which would otherwise be indistinguishable from a genuinely quiet week in the per-user rows

coins_credited.notes: any CoinLedgerEntry credit. props amount, balance_after, replayed. Emitted per ledger movement with the description deliberately NOT logged: descriptions are free text assembled from catalog titles and species names, and the business reason is already carried by the event that triggered the credit (attendance_recorded, streak_week_resulted, sprout_caught, coins_refunded). replayed=true is an idempotent re-run, not new currency

coins_debited.notes: props amount, balance_after, replayed. See coins_credited for why the description is excluded

coins_catalog_viewed.notes: props item_count. The marketplace impression; the gap between this and coins_redeemed is the catalog drop-off

coins_redeemed.notes: props path (wallet | customer), redemption_id, category, coin_cost, discount_amount, replayed. path separates wallet-service's redemption inside a subscription purchase from the customer's own marketplace redemption, which have entirely different economics: one discounts a purchase already being made, the other spends coins for something on its own

coins_redemption_rejected.notes: props path, reason (gym_trial_cap_reached | gym_trial_already_claimed | insufficient_coins). Recorded from the catch rather than the throw site, because a serializable-transaction retry can roll a rejection back and then succeed. The most actionable event in the coin layer: an insufficient_coins spike means the earn rate is too tight for the catalog's prices, and gym_trial_cap_reached means the month's supply is gone

coins_refunded.notes: props redemption_id, coin_cost, already_refunded. Coins clawed back because the downstream subscription purchase failed after the debit. A rising count means that purchase flow is breaking, and it is the signal that coins are not being burned for nothing

workout_credited.notes: health-service asked whether a finished workout session earns coins. props verified, credited, amount, economy_disabled. verified=false means no AttendanceEventLog row for that user today, so the workout and check-in surfaces have drifted apart. This is the most useful diagnostic in the file because it fires for every workout logged without a check-in

paired_streak_opted_in.notes: props match_id, already. This build auto-enrolls both members rather than having an invite/accept sub-flow, so a single event is emitted for whoever tapped

paired_streak_week_closed.notes: one anonymous row per cron run, alongside streak_week_closed. props week_start, pairs, survived, broken. A pair survives only if both members independently qualified, so this measures whether the mechanic holds up or just punishes the weaker half of every pair

sprouts_nearby_viewed.notes: props challenge_id, spawn_count, seeded_count. seeded_count > 0 means this read had to mint spawns to reach the live minimum, so ordinary reads are also what keep the map populated

sprout_caught.notes: props challenge_id, spawn_id, caught, reason (already_gone | too_far | lost_race | null), species_key, rarity, coins_awarded, distance_bucket. Every non-catch is recorded with its cause: too_far means the spawn was visible but out of reach (a spawn-radius or client-GPS problem), already_gone and lost_race are other users winning it. distance_bucket is rounded to 100m and capped at 50 so it can never become a location log
